title.narrative: World Bank PID Trust Fund for Palestine 2023-2026
World Bank PID Trust Fund för Palestina 2023-2026

description.narrative: The Partnership for Infrastructure Development (PID) Multi Donor Trust Fund's (MDTF) Project Development objective is to improve coverage, quality and sustainability of infrastructure in Palestine in the water, urban development and energy sectors. The design of the program is intended to support the core principles of sustainability, partnership, client-driven ownership, harmonization, and knowledge building. The PID MDTF predominantly provides co-financing to investment operations implemented by the Palestinian Authority (PA). The PID MDTF supports the PA to achieve its sectoral objectives to improving basic service delivery and performance across the water, energy and urban development sectors. Projects co-financed by the PID MDTF focus both on infrastructure financing and capacity building with the objective to improve service delivery, strengthen key institutions, and advance critical sector reforms. The Trust Fund (TF) provides financing for infrastructure projects and programs, and analytical and advisory activities that the World Bank (WB) is supporting in the water, urban development, and energy sectors. The operations in the TF are according to the WBs support for the PAs strategic long-term plans for development.

Det övergripande utvecklingsmålet för World Bank Partnership for Infrastructure Development Multi-Donor Trust Fund (PID MDTF) är att förbättra täckningen, kvaliteten och hållbarheten för infrastrukturen i Palestina (som inte är i område C) genom ekonomiskt och tekniskt bistånd till Palestinian Authority (PA) för utveckling av infrastruktur och relaterad kapacitetsuppbyggnad och institutionell utveckling inom vatten-, stadsutvecklings- och energisektorerna. Fonden stöder PA:s ansträngningar att genomföra den nationella utvecklingsplanen (NDP) 2021-2023.

The overall development objective for the World Bank Partnership for Infrastructure Development Multi-Donor Trust Fund (PID MDTF) is to improve the coverage, quality, and sustainability of infrastructure in Palestine (that is not in area C) through financial and technical assistance to the Palestinian Authority (PA) for infrastructure development and related capacity building and institutional development in the water, urban development, and energy sectors. The Trust Fund supports the PA’s efforts to implement the National Development Plan (NDP) 2021-2023.

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The PID MDTF work in Gaza has been severely hampered by the war. Selection of results and updates for 2023/24 below.
Urban and Land Sector
THIRD MUNICIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (MDP-3) The RMSP became effective on August 15, 2023. Municipalities are struggling to provide essential services to citizens during the conflict; the World Bank is working with the Municipal Development and Lending Fund (MDLF) to identify options. A restructuring and additional financing to provide an emergency support to municipalities in the West Bank is in preparation to restore essential services as soon as possible.
RESILIENT MUNICIPAL SERVICES PROJECT (RMSP) The RERP has made strong progress and will close satisfactorily: some 147,000 properties have now been registered against the end target of some 162,000. However, property registration has been delayed since the start of the conflict by the suspension of activities of the settlement courts. The closing date is November 30, 2024.
Water Sector
ASSOCIATED WORKS PHASE I (AWP-1) Substantial progress and improvement on disbursement before October 7. All works in Gaza have stopped and the project is being restructured to reallocate $9 million of uncommitted funds towards the immediate water needs.
WASTEWATER MANAGEMENT SUSTAINABILITY (WMS) PROJECT The operation of the NGWWTP wastewater plant has been suspended since October 7th, 2023. The project is being restructured to extend the Project closing date for 18 months to December 30, 2025. According to latest satellite imagery, there are no observable damages to the main infrastructure.
EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN AND RECOVERY ROADMAP The World Bank, in coordination Development Partners, is supporting the PWA to provide a framework for planning for the emergency response and recovery and reconstruction of the water sector.
2025-06-26
Results:
Water
Project AWP 1: Most project activities have been interrupted since October 2023. Closing date extended to December 1, 2025. Project restructured to reallocate $9 million for urgent needs: $7 million for UNICEF to provide water tanks, hygiene kits, fuel, and support for critical WASH facilities (disbursed). $2 million for UNDP to provide equipment and water tanker trucks (disbursement now complete). Progress being made under Component 2 (capacity building) with contracts signed for the design of Tulkarem and Northeast Ramallah Wastewater Treatment Plants
WMS Closing date extended to December 31, 2025 Project continued to be halted due to the conflict. North Gaza Wastewater Treatment Plant (NGWWT) has been inaccessible to date after the ceasefire. Early rehabilitation and recommissioning would be a priority if the situation allows.
WSRP Despite delays related to the situation in Jenin, procurement for component 1 is advancing. Requests for Bids have been issued across Packages 1 3, and bid opening expected by end of March Component 2 o Completion of the Strategic Planning and Sector Reform Literature Review of Laws, Regulations, Policies, and Strategies Synthesis Report in June 2024. o Terms of Reference under discussion to establish the Marj Ibn Amer Regional Water Utility (MIAWU), consolidating existing providers into a unified regional utility.
Urban and Land sectors
RMSP RMSP restructured in June 2024. Focus shifted solely to the West Bank with reallocation of funds among project components. Implementation is progressing well. The Municipal Development and Lending Fund had preapproved and approved 165 subprojects out of 171. 54 subprojects are ongoing on the ground and 46 subprojects completed.
RERP RERP exceeded the target number of registered properties of 161,804 properties by 7,710 additional titles (105%). Registration time for properties through the Systematic Land Registration process has fallen from 10.5 months to 5 months exceeding targets. Completion of PLA Digital Transformation Strategy. Project closing date has been extended from March 31, 2025 to September 30, 2025. Based on the success of RERP, a second phase project is under preparation.
ISWMP1 Approved by the Board of Directors on January 30, 2025 Declaration of effectiveness is underway First phase of a Series of Projects to address WB&Gs complex SWM sector issues, major infrastructure deficits, and incremental policy reform needed to support the improved solid waste management.
ASA Tech Ass The net lending action plan is finalized the international consultant conducted a virtual mission to the West Bank in December 2024 and has presented the report findings to PA stakeholders and development partners The Solid Waste Management Roadmap for WB&G has been finalized, and its dissemination workshop was conducted in August 2024. The roadmap informed the ISWMP1 preparation and the PAs new National Solid Waste Management Strategy (NSWMS) (2025-2029)
Energy
ASPIRE MPA
Phase I progress: 45 km of MV lines were upgraded and constructed in West Bank. Solar systems with a total capacity of 667.8 kWp were installed in six health facilities. RFQs for private sector solar IPPs were launched on March 3rd, 2025, under the LSAPS activity. Deployment of smart meters across the five electricity distribution companies in the West Bank. Full integration of smart meters is expected by June 2025.
Phase II progress: Project implementation continues but with progress affected by logistical uncertainties Several contracts for the supply of goods in Gaza have been signed, others remain on hold due to entry restrictions. In the interim, goods are being delivered to PENRAs warehouses in the West Bank, pending conditions that will allow their transport to Gaza and endorsement of resumption of basic services by Board of Director.
Phase III progress: Advancing to the Board for approval on April 8, 2025. Proposed project builds on the momentum and achievements of previous ASPIRE phases. Aims to enhance the operational and financial performance of energy sector institutions and diversify energy sources.
Crosscutting activities in Gender, Climate and Citizen Engagement are quite ambitious.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
